p.src: Now Zhang He had divided his thirty thousand troops among three strongholds, each protected by mountainous terrain: Dangqu Stockade, Mengtou Stockade, and Dangshi Stockade. That day, Zhang He took half the troops from each stronghold to seize Baxi, leaving the other half to defend the stockades. Scouts soon reached Baxi with word that Zhang He was approaching at the head of an army. Zhang Fei hastily summoned Lei Tong to confer. Lei Tong said, “The country around Langzhong is rugged and mountainous, well suited to an ambush. Lead your troops out to meet him, General, and I shall aid you with a surprise force. Then Zhang He can be captured.”

p.src: Zhang Fei assigned five thousand picked troops to Lei Tong, who departed with them. Zhang Fei himself led ten thousand men and, thirty li from Langzhong, encountered Zhang He’s army. The two armies deployed. Zhang Fei rode forth and challenged Zhang He to single combat. Zhang He leveled his spear and galloped out. After more than thirty bouts, a sudden clamor arose in Zhang He’s rear ranks. They had caught sight of Shu banners behind the mountain and were thrown into confusion. Zhang He dared not prolong the fight; he wheeled his horse and fled. Zhang Fei charged after him from the rear. Ahead, Lei Tong led his troops out to attack as well. Attacked from both sides, Zhang He’s army suffered a crushing defeat. Zhang Fei and Lei Tong pursued through the night, driving the enemy all the way to Mount Dangqu. Zhang He again divided his troops among the three strongholds, laying in many rolling logs and catapult stones, and held fast without offering battle. Zhang Fei encamped ten li from Dangqu and led his troops out to challenge the next day. On the mountain Zhang He feasted and drank amid a great din of pipes and drums, but would not descend. Zhang Fei ordered his soldiers to heap abuse upon him, but Zhang He still refused to emerge. Zhang Fei had no choice but to return to camp.

p.src: The next day, Lei Tong again went beneath the mountain to issue a challenge. Again Zhang He would not come out. Lei Tong drove his soldiers up the mountain, but logs and stones came crashing down from above. Lei Tong hastily retreated. Troops from the Dangshi and Mengtou stockades sallied out and defeated him. The following day, Zhang Fei went forth to challenge them again. Zhang He still would not emerge. Zhang Fei had his men revile him in every filthy fashion, and Zhang He answered with curses from the mountain. Zhang Fei pondered but could devise no means against him. The standoff lasted more than fifty days. Zhang Fei established a large camp before the mountain and drank wine every day; when thoroughly drunk, he would sit before the mountain and shout insults.

p.src: Xuande sent a man to reward the troops; seeing Zhang Fei drink all day, the envoy returned and reported it to Xuande. Xuande was greatly alarmed and hurried to consult Kongming. Kongming laughed. “So that is what has happened. I fear there is no fine wine at the front. Chengdu has excellent vintages in abundance. Load fifty jars onto three carts and send them to General Zhang to drink at the front.” Xuande said, “My brother has always brought trouble upon himself through drink. Why, Strategist, would you send him even more?” Kongming laughed. “My lord, after so many years as Yide’s sworn brother, do you still not know what kind of man he is? Yide has always been fierce and unyielding, yet during the conquest of Shu he released Yan Yan out of respect for his righteousness. That was no mere brute warrior’s act. Now he has faced Zhang He for more than fifty days, and after getting drunk sits before the mountain hurling insults as though no one else were there. This is not a craving for the cup, but a scheme to defeat Zhang He.” Xuande said, “Even so, we must not be overconfident. Let Wei Yan go to assist him.” Kongming ordered Wei Yan to escort the wine to the front. Each cart bore a yellow banner inscribed in large characters: “Fine Wine for Official Army Use.” Wei Yan obeyed and escorted the wine to the camp. When he met Zhang Fei, he conveyed that their lord had bestowed the wine. Zhang Fei bowed to receive it, then ordered Wei Yan and Lei Tong each to lead a force as the left and right wings; when they saw a red flag rise in the camp, each was to advance. He had the wine set out below his tent and ordered the soldiers to drink openly amid a great display of banners and drums.

p.src: A spy reported this on the mountain, and Zhang He came in person to the summit to observe. He saw Zhang Fei seated beneath his tent drinking, while two young soldiers wrestled before him for amusement. Zhang He said, “Zhang Fei insults me beyond endurance!” He ordered a night descent to raid Zhang Fei’s camp. He also ordered the Mengtou and Dangshi garrisons to sally out in support on his left and right. That night, under the faint moonlight, Zhang He led his army down the mountainside and went straight to the enemy camp. From afar he saw Zhang Fei’s camp brilliantly lit with lamps and candles, and Zhang Fei drinking inside his tent. Zhang He gave a great shout at the fore; drums thundered before the mountain in support, and he charged straight into the central camp. There sat Zhang Fei, perfectly motionless. Zhang He galloped up and thrust his spear, only to find that it was a straw dummy. As he hastily reined about, a succession of signal blasts erupted behind the tent. A general barred his retreat, eyes round and glaring, voice like mighty thunder: it was Zhang Fei. Leveling his spear and spurring his horse, he charged straight at Zhang He. Amid the firelight, the two generals fought for some thirty to fifty bouts. Zhang He counted only on relief from the two stockades, unaware that Wei Yan and Lei Tong had already repulsed their troops and seized both strongholds in the same stroke. When no relief appeared, Zhang He was at his wits’ end. Then he saw flames rise on the mountain: Zhang Fei’s rear force had already taken his main stockade. Having lost all three strongholds, Zhang He could only flee to Wakou Pass. Zhang Fei won a resounding victory, and the report was sent to Chengdu. Xuande rejoiced greatly and only then understood that Yide’s drinking had been a stratagem meant to lure Zhang He down from the mountain.

p.src: Now Zhang He withdrew to defend Wakou Pass. Of his thirty thousand troops, twenty thousand had been lost, so he sent a man to Cao Hong to request aid. Cao Hong was furious. “You would not heed my words but insisted on advancing. Now you have lost vital passes and come asking me for aid!” He refused to dispatch troops and instead sent a man to press Zhang He to give battle. Zhang He grew anxious and had no choice but to devise a plan. He divided two forces and concealed them in remote mountain ground before the pass. He instructed them, “I shall feign defeat. Zhang Fei is certain to pursue; then cut off his retreat.”

p.src: That day, Zhang He led his army forward and encountered Lei Tong. After only a few bouts, Zhang He fled in defeat, and Lei Tong pursued. The two hidden forces emerged together and cut off his way back. Zhang He turned back and speared Lei Tong from his horse. The defeated soldiers returned and reported to Zhang Fei. Zhang Fei came in person to challenge Zhang He. Zhang He again feigned defeat, but Zhang Fei did not pursue. Zhang He returned to fight, then fled again after only a few bouts. Zhang Fei recognized the scheme, withdrew to camp, and conferred with Wei Yan. “Zhang He used an ambush to kill Lei Tong and now seeks to ensnare me as well. Why should we not turn his own stratagem against him?” Wei Yan asked, “How?” Zhang Fei said, “Tomorrow I shall lead one force ahead, while you follow with picked troops. When the ambushers appear, divide your men and strike them. Use more than ten carts, each loaded with concealed firewood, to block the narrow road, then set them alight. I shall seize the opportunity to capture Zhang He and avenge Lei Tong.” Wei Yan accepted the plan. The next day, Zhang Fei led his troops forward. Zhang He’s troops appeared again and engaged Zhang Fei. After ten bouts, Zhang He again feigned defeat. Zhang Fei pursued with horse and foot, while Zhang He fought as he retreated. After luring Zhang Fei past the mouth of the valley, Zhang He brought his rear ranks to the front, established a new camp, and fought Zhang Fei once more. He expected the two bodies of ambushers to emerge and surround Zhang Fei. But unexpectedly Wei Yan’s picked troops reached the ambushers first and drove them into the valley. They used the carts to block the mountain road and set them ablaze; the valley’s grass and trees all caught fire, smoke obscured the paths, and the soldiers could not escape. Zhang Fei pressed his army relentlessly through the enemy. Zhang He was utterly defeated and fought desperately to open a path, fled up to Wakou Pass, gathered his surviving troops, and held fast without emerging.

p.src: For several days, Zhang Fei and Wei Yan attacked the pass but failed to take it. Seeing that their efforts were of no avail, Zhang Fei withdrew the army twenty li, then took Wei Yan and several dozen horsemen to scout the lesser paths on both sides. Suddenly they saw several men and women, each carrying a small bundle, making their way along a remote mountain path by clinging to vines and creepers. Pointing at them with his whip from horseback, Zhang Fei said to Wei Yan, “The taking of Wakou Pass depends upon those few commoners.” He called his soldiers over and ordered them, “Do not frighten them. Gently bring those commoners here.” The soldiers hastened to summon them before his horse. Zhang Fei reassured them with kindly words and asked where they had come from. The commoners replied, “We are all residents of Hanzhong and now wish to return home. We heard that the armies were fighting and that the main road through Langzhong had been blocked; so we are passing through Cangxi and will enter Hanzhong by way of Zitong Mountain and Huijin River to return to our homes.” Zhang Fei asked, “How far is Wakou Pass by this road?” The commoners replied, “The lesser path through Zitong Mountain comes out behind Wakou Pass.” Zhang Fei was delighted. He took the commoners back to camp, gave them food and wine, and ordered Wei Yan to lead troops in an assault upon the front of the pass. “I shall personally take light cavalry through Zitong Mountain and attack its rear.” He then made the commoners guide him, selected five hundred light horsemen, and advanced along the lesser path.

p.src: Meanwhile, Zhang He was brooding because no reinforcements had arrived. A messenger reported, “Wei Yan is attacking below the pass.” Zhang He donned his armor, mounted his horse, and was about to descend the mountain when another report suddenly came: “Fires have broken out along four or five routes behind the pass. We do not know where those troops have come from.” Zhang He personally led troops to meet them. As the banners parted, he saw Zhang Fei already before him. Zhang He was greatly alarmed and hurriedly fled down a narrow path, but the way was too rough for his horse. Zhang Fei pursued hard behind him. Zhang He abandoned his horse, climbed the mountain, and escaped by seeking out a footpath. With only a little over ten followers remaining, he entered Nanzheng on foot and presented himself before Cao Hong. When Cao Hong saw that Zhang He had only a little over ten men left, he flew into a rage and said, “I told you not to go, yet you insisted upon obtaining a written warrant so that you could depart; today you have lost the entire army. Why have you not killed yourself? What have you come back for?” He shouted for his attendants to drag Zhang He out and behead him. Guo Huai, the Army Marshal, remonstrated: “An army of ten thousand is easily raised, but a good general is hard to find. Though Zhang He is guilty, he is deeply valued by the King of Wei and must not be summarily executed. Give him another five thousand troops and have him strike directly at Jiameng Pass. By drawing the enemy’s forces from the surrounding regions, Hanzhong will be secure. If he does not succeed, punish him for both offenses together.” Cao Hong accepted this counsel, gave Zhang He another five thousand troops, and ordered him to take Jiameng Pass. Zhang He received the order and departed.

p.src: Meanwhile, Meng Da and Huo Jun, the commanders guarding Jiameng Pass, learned that Zhang He’s army was approaching. Huo Jun wished only to hold the pass firmly, but Meng Da insisted upon meeting the enemy. Meng Da led troops down from the pass and engaged Zhang He, but suffered a crushing defeat and returned. Huo Jun urgently sent a dispatch to Chengdu. When Xuande heard the news, he summoned the Military Adviser to discuss it. Kongming assembled the generals in the hall and said, “Jiameng Pass is now in grave danger. We must recall Yide from Langzhong before Zhang He can be repelled.” Fa Zheng said, “Yide’s troops are now stationed at Wakou, guarding Langzhong, which is also a vital position. He cannot be recalled. Choose one of the generals here in camp and send him to defeat Zhang He.” Kongming smiled and said, “Zhang He is a renowned general of Wei, beyond the reach of ordinary men. No one but Yide can withstand him.” Suddenly one man strode forward and cried sternly, “Why does the Military Adviser think so little of us all? Though I am a man of little ability, I am willing to cut off Zhang He’s head and lay it before your command.”

p.src: They looked and saw that it was the veteran general Huang Zhong. Kongming said, “Though Hansheng is valiant, you are old. I fear you are no match for Zhang He.” Hearing this, Huang Zhong’s white beard bristled as he declared, “Though I am old, my arms can still draw a bow of three shi, and my body still possesses the strength of a thousand jin. How could I be unable to match that fellow Zhang He?” Kongming said, “General, you are nearly seventy. How can you claim not to be old?” Huang Zhong hurried down from the hall, took a great saber from its rack, and whirled it as swiftly as flight; then he seized the stout bows hanging on the wall and snapped two of them in succession as he drew them. Kongming asked, “If you are to go, General, who shall serve as your deputy?” Huang Zhong replied, “The veteran general Yan Yan may go with me. If any mishap occurs, you may take this white head of mine first.” Xuande was delighted and at once ordered Yan Yan and Huang Zhong to go and engage Zhang He. Zhao Yun remonstrated, “Zhang He himself is now attacking Jiameng Pass. Military Adviser, you must not treat this as a child’s game. If Jiameng Pass should fall, Yizhou will be in peril. Why send two aged generals against such a formidable foe?” Kongming replied, “You think that these two are too old to accomplish anything, but I foresee that Hanzhong itself will surely be won through their hands.” Zhao Yun and the others withdrew, each laughing scornfully.

p.src: When Huang Zhong and Yan Yan arrived at the pass, Meng Da and Huo Jun saw them and inwardly laughed at Kongming’s poor judgment: “How could he send only two old men to such a vital place?” Huang Zhong said to Yan Yan, “Did you notice how everyone behaved? They laugh at us for being old. Now we must perform an extraordinary feat and win them all over.” Yan Yan replied, “I await your orders, General.” After the two had settled their plan, Huang Zhong led troops down from the pass and drew up against Zhang He. Zhang He rode out. Seeing Huang Zhong, he laughed and said, “At your great age, have you still no sense of shame? Do you yet mean to take the field?” Huang Zhong angrily cried, “Impudent whelp, you mock me for my age! But the treasured saber in my hand has not grown old!” He spurred his horse forward and fought Zhang He. Their horses crossed, and after they had fought for more than twenty bouts, battle cries suddenly arose behind Zhang He. It was Yan Yan, who had taken a lesser path and circled behind Zhang He’s army. Attacked from both sides, Zhang He suffered a crushing defeat. They pursued him through the night, and Zhang He’s troops retreated eighty or ninety li. Huang Zhong and Yan Yan then recalled their troops to camp, where both held their forces back without further movement.

p.src: When Cao Hong learned that Zhang He had lost another engagement, he again wished to punish him. Guo Huai said, “If Zhang He is driven too hard, he will surely defect to Western Shu. You should now send generals to support him and, while they are nearby, supervise him so that he entertains no disloyal thoughts.” Cao Hong accepted this advice and immediately dispatched Xiahou Shang, a nephew of Xiahou Dun, together with Han Hao, the brother of the surrendered general Han Xuan. The two led five thousand troops to support the fighting. The two generals set out at once. Upon reaching Zhang He’s camp, they asked about the military situation. Zhang He said, “The veteran general Huang Zhong is a formidable warrior; and with Yan Yan assisting him, we must not underestimate the enemy.” Han Hao said, “I knew the prowess of that old villain when I was in Changsha. He and Wei Yan surrendered the city and brought about my elder brother’s death. Now that I have met him, I must avenge that wrong.” He and Xiahou Shang then led the fresh troops out of camp and advanced.

By daybreak, three camps had been taken in succession. Countless weapons, saddles, and horses had been abandoned in the camps, and Meng Da was ordered to transport them all into the pass. Huang Zhong urged his forces onward in pursuit. Zhang He’s troops were thrown into confusion by their own routed men. Unable to hold their positions, they fled to the rear, abandoning many stockades and camps, and ran all the way to the bank of the Han River.
